source.credit: Oberst et al. (2001), Icarus 153, 16–23; Buratti et al. (2004), Icarus 167, 129–135, Table 1

constraints.axisConvention: Full axes are halved exactly. +Z is the adopted pole; +X is the arbitrary display meridian.
constraints.qualification: Ellipsoid approximation of the published 2.1 × 1 × 1 km size estimate combining Deep Space 1 images and ground-based photometry. The equal short axes are part of that coarse estimate; resolved local terrain is not represented.
constraints.scale: The reference radius is the geometric mean of the approximation semiaxes. It is a rendering scale, not an independent measured mean radius or convex-model volume.

assumptions: Ellipsoid approximation of the published 2.1 × 1 × 1 km size estimate combining Deep Space 1 images and ground-based photometry. The equal short axes are part of that coarse estimate; resolved local terrain is not represented.
Arbitrary display pole and meridian. The published 226.4 ± 1.3 h estimate is synodic and is not installed as a sidereal spin or an observed pole.
approximation.qualification: Observation-constrained ellipsoid; no invented local terrain or albedo.

spin.meaning: Arbitrary display pole and meridian. The published 226.4 ± 1.3 h estimate is synodic and is not installed as a sidereal spin or an observed pole.

unresolved: Original closed global mesh and registered surface imagery remain unresolved in the checked DS1 archive.
Integrated infrared spectra constrain composition, not the position of surface texels.
The quoted period is a probable synodic solution, not a qualified sidereal attitude model.
The arbitrary display pole and meridian are not measured orientation.
